<reason>PRO built the cleaner path on the motion as written: public language and liberal operating rules as non-optional civic infrastructure, with opportunity failing if the host makes remaining outside costless. CON’s best weapon was the “what does expectation add?” trap and the two-tier charge, and those rebuttals were sharper, but CON’s honest answer that large voting blocs may demand courts and schools in a private tongue as ordinary politics conceded the language clash. Civic-norms examples mostly collapsed into existing law; the surviving, vote-moving comparison was unequal public membership if the common tongue is optional.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO asked whether never-adopting the public language extends to large voting populations; CON said yes, as ordinary pluralism (Finland/Belgium/multilingual ballots). PRO then weighed that as emptying equal membership of public content—the exchange that decided the live clash.</best_rebuttal>
